A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ChronoSense study. Their complete main texts, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of seven LLMs on Allen relations and temporal arithmetic, including prompting, event-abstraction and prompt-variation experiments.

after.justification: v2 reports original evaluations of seven LLMs, revised quantitative results and additional qualitative failure examples in the appendix.

M1.justification: The proposed benchmark retains its template-based question generation, Wikidata event pairs, synthetic arithmetic questions and negative-relation exclusions. Newly documented prompting and filtering details do not establish a change to the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 13 Allen relations and three temporal arithmetic tasks, using real event names and abstract names with year-level temporal information. The larger test sets change sample counts, not task or domain coverage.

E2.justification: The reported Gemma comparator changes from Gemma2-9B, linked to the base checkpoint in v1, to Gemma2-9B-it, linked to the instruction-tuned checkpoint in v2. The other six comparators remain, including in the full appendix comparisons.

E3.justification: Section 3 changes the stated test set from 50 to 500 examples per task, substantially expanding evaluation sample sizes. Training and validation counts remain 4,000 and 500; the zero-, one-, three-shot and CoT settings and 64/512-token output limits are retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds an illustrative error analysis in Appendix A.5 and Table 12, with six selected model responses plus a separate temporal-granularity example. It also flags results with many unclear answers. The existing event-abstraction and prompt-variant analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report mean accuracy and standard deviation across three prompt variants, in v1 Table 10 and v2 Table 11. Neither adds repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: Numerical results are extensively replaced. For example, Llama3.1-8B's one-/three-shot Allen averages change from 0.54/0.60 in v1 Table 3 to 0.01/0.01 in v2 Table 1. The hardest CoT relation changes from Overlapped-By to Equals. These are revised outcomes under different reported test sizes, rather than directly comparable performance changes.

T1.justification: v1 Section 2.1 formally defines the five-field event tuple, its interval and the duration calculation; v2 removes this formalization. The 13 Allen relations and the illustrative transitivity argument remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain the 16-task ChronoSense benchmark, seven-model evaluation, investigation of prompting effects and possible reliance on memorized event knowledge. The rewritten abstract, contribution bullets and conclusion preserve these main claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds failure-mechanism interpretations, links endpoint matching to difficult relations and discusses implications for historical, legal and medical applications. It qualifies abstract-name degradation as affecting most models. Section 7 removes both the small-test-set caveat and the limitation concerning explicit years in real-world scenarios.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies dated GPT checkpoints, the exact CoT instruction, data-filtering information and computational resources, runtime and API-cost bounds in Appendix A.4. However, it omits v1's precise rule marking responses containing both or neither answer string as invalid and incorrect.

R1.justification: v2 adds Kojima et al. (2022) for zero-shot CoT prompting and Tang and Belle (2024) for LTLBench. The existing benchmark landscape and positioning around comprehensive coverage of all 13 Allen relations remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 substantially compresses and rewrites the introduction, dataset description, experiments, related work and conclusion. It replaces several numbered subsections with inline headings, moves question-generation details into Appendix A.1 and consolidates experimental discussion into a general-findings narrative.

P2.justification: v2 reorganizes the main results into a combined summary and a selected three-model table, relocates complete comparisons and question templates to the appendix, and adds the failure-case table. Tables gain reordered rows and unclear-answer markers. Both figures retain their image content but are resized and receive shorter captions.

improvement.justification: The expanded test sets address v1's explicitly acknowledged small-sample limitation, while the new failure examples and computational and prompting details improve interpretation and reproducibility. These gains support a limited net improvement. The benefits are tempered by omission of the precise invalid-answer scoring rule and the explicit-year applicability caveat, with substantial response-format failures still affecting the evaluation.
